metadata.description: Installable package kind (VIBEVM-SPEC §4.1). Open vocabulary: the register grows by owner amendment, so a reader must not hard-fail on an unseen kind.
Subskill materialisation mode. Open vocabulary: modes are a growing register, not a closed set.

Repository naming convention mapping a pkgref to a repo name (PROP-008 §2.5). Closed vocabulary: repository paths are built from these values, so an unfamiliar one has no safe behaviour. The four wire strings are explicit per-variant renames, not one rename rule — `kind-name` and `kind/name` are not derivable from a single case convention. That same fact is why `x-rust-variants` exists here: from `kind/name` the generator mints a collision-suffixed identifier over the one it already gave `kind-name`, and no case rule produces a meaningful name — so the name is DECLARED rather than derived, keyed by the wire value both sides carry verbatim. (A description becomes a doc comment in the emitted file and passes through the very renames the code does, so quoting a pre-rename identifier here would leave the emitted doc naming something that no longer exists.) Two copies exist in code (`vibe-index/src/types/kinds.rs` and `vibe-core/src/manifest/project.rs`) with identical strings today; the index-side test `naming_convention_serde_matches_vibe_core_wire` pins them, and Phase 4.2 converges the copies. Shared as a vocabulary because `repomd` and `journal` both carry it.
Reverse-FQDN namespace qualifier (PROP-008 §2.1) — the `vibe_core::Group` newtype on the wire.
Semantic version string — `semver::Version` in code.
RFC 3339 timestamp — `chrono::DateTime<Utc>` in code.
One lifecycle contribution execution, shared by the generic lifecycle and native context roots.
Actual dependency or host provider identity, without an invented package coordinate for an ungrouped host.
Effective handler configuration after whole-value host activation override.
The selected project identity and source roots supplied to a lifecycle or native handler.
One selected package in the resolved lifecycle world.
The lockfile, dependency root and selected packages visible to a lifecycle or native handler.
Selected reachable packages in canonical lockfile order.
Closed invocation mode for a lifecycle/native handler run.
The requested lifecycle chain and execution controls supplied to a handler.
One accumulated lifecycle artifact supplied as handler input. The engine-owned `phase` distinguishes it from a reply artifact.
The package slot targeted by a pre/post-install contribution.
Invocation-local IO paths supplied to a lifecycle or native handler.
One artifact declared by a lifecycle or native reply. It deliberately omits the engine-owned accumulated `phase`.
Closed lifecycle/native handler reply outcome.

One measured duration: microseconds plus an explicit saturation marker. `micros` saturates at u32::MAX rather than wrapping; `saturated` is true when the measurement hit that ceiling (or contributed to a total that did) — so the marker is legal ONLY at `micros = u32::MAX`, while an unsaturated `u32::MAX` stays legal because an exact measurement may land exactly there. Writer-side saturation policy lands with the recorder; the representable form is pinned here. Shared as a vocabulary because the trace index, the timing row and every command report's trace member carry the SAME record (JTD has no cross-file refs, G9).

One row of the CLI timing table: everything the run spent on one pass name, recomputable from `events` — the validator never trusts the carried totals. Shared as a vocabulary so the trace index and every command report's trace member use ONE generated `TimingRow`, not same-shaped per-module types that would need converters.
Exact pass name this row aggregates.
How many events carry this pass name.
Saturating sum of the pass durations this pass name's events carry.
Saturating sum of the verify durations.
Saturating sum of the encode durations.

The trace half of one command report: what the observer knows when the report is built. Closed: an unknown spelling is a reader error, not a newer writer — additive evolution of this record rides new object members, never new status values.

The ONE shared trace member every command report root carries (install, lifecycle, update, reinstall): the run's trace identity, its terminal state, lossless canonical-decimal counts and the same timing rows the CLI table prints. Disabled old JSON simply omits the member; `unavailable` is the honest word when tracing was requested but no recorder could be opened — the command still compiles untraced. The relational laws JTD cannot express are named in `x-relational-laws` and enforced by the hand-written validator in `vibe-wire/src/behaviour/compile_trace_report/`; the two label sets are pinned equal by a wire test, so an undocumented law and an unimplemented label are both red.
x-relational-laws: run-id: `run_id` is exactly 32 lowercase hex characters — the same law the trace index and the lifecycle state hold the id to

canonical-counts: `events`, `snapshots` and `snapshot_bytes` are CANONICAL unsigned decimal strings — nonempty, ASCII digits only, and no leading zero unless the whole value is `0`. JTD has no uint64; a count is never narrowed through a usize/u64 or a lossy float on either side of the wire

run-path: `run_path`, when present, is ABSOLUTE, forward-slashed (no backslash, no CR/LF/NUL anywhere) and ends with `.vibe/trace/<run_id>`. This law owns only HOW a present path is spelled; WHEN one exists belongs to `status-matrix`, which enforces it from both directions

status-matrix: `run_path` is present exactly for the ACTIVE statuses — `running`, `ok` and `failed` each name their directory, `unavailable` carries none. `unavailable` is furthermore not finalised, not budget-exhausted (a recorder that never opened never owned a snapshot budget), carries zero events/snapshots/snapshot-bytes, no timing rows, and at least one NONBLANK bounded warning saying why (a vector of empty or whitespace-only strings is not a diagnostic; the nonblank rule is the unavailable-reason law and is not extended to an active run's warnings). `running` is not finalised; `ok` and `failed` are finalised
count-coherence: `snapshots` ≤ `events`, compared as canonical decimals (length, then lexicographic) — never by narrowing to a machine integer
warning-cap: every warning is at most the shared diagnostic cap (`x-diagnostic-cap-bytes`)

timing-rows: pass names are unique and non-blank, and every duration is canonical in the compiler-trace aggregate sense (`saturated` only at `micros = u32::MAX`); the totals algorithm stays the index's — this record carries rows, it never recomputes them

metadata.description: The trace's state at report time: `unavailable` (requested, never opened), `running` (parked mid-run), `ok`/`failed` (finalised).
The lifecycle run that owns the trace — the exact 32-lowercase-hex `RunMetadata.run_id`. Even `unavailable` carries the id: the run existed, only its trace did not.
True exactly when the trace index reached a terminal state (`ok`/`failed`); a parked or never-opened trace is not finalised.

True when the run's snapshot-byte budget was spent and later invocations stood down as `snapshot-skipped-budget`. Always false for `unavailable`: a recorder that never opened never owned a budget to spend.
How many pass events the trace recorded — a canonical unsigned decimal string (JTD has no uint64).
How many certified snapshot files the trace published — a canonical unsigned decimal string, at most `events`.
Total snapshot payload bytes — a canonical unsigned decimal string.
The same aggregate timing rows the CLI table prints, in the index's first-appearance order. Explicit even when empty.
Bounded observer warnings — a requested-but-unavailable open, a scope failure the trace survived. Explicit even when empty (except `unavailable`, which must carry at least one NONBLANK reason).

Absolute forward-slashed path of `.vibe/trace/<run_id>`. Present for every ACTIVE status (`running`, `ok`, `failed`) and absent exactly when the trace never opened (`unavailable`) — the optionality is the closed status vocabulary's, not the writer's choice.

The closed five-value evidence-comparison vocabulary (PROP-054 `##EVIDENCE-OUTCOME-VOCABULARY`). `matched` is the ONLY pass; `stale` is a digest or declaration mismatch, `missing` an owed observation that is absent, `unavailable` an honestly undeclared or legacy witness, and `unstable` a source that moved while it was being observed. Closed: an unknown spelling is a reader error, not a newer writer — evidence evolves by new object members, never by a sixth outcome word. The words `unmet`, `met`, `fulfilled` and `verified` are deliberately ABSENT (`##REQUIREMENT-OBSERVATION-AXES`): combining the observation axes into a next-work verdict is the external orchestrator's policy, never this wire's.

One content witness: the algorithm that produced it, the digest itself, and — for the manifest forms that count what they covered — how many files and bytes entered it. `files` and `bytes` are ONE PAIR: both present or both absent, never one alone. They are present exactly for the input-manifest form and absent exactly for the artifact forms that need no counts (a regular file's witness IS its bytes; a directory's is its canonical manifest), so their presence is part of a witness's shape — the `witness-shape` law reads it from both directions, or `matched` would compare two different kinds of claim. `bytes` is a CANONICAL UNSIGNED DECIMAL STRING, not a narrowed integer: JTD has no `uint64`, and a declared input set above 4 GiB must stay representable, so the count rides the same lossless spelling the compile-trace member's counts already use and no reader parses it into a machine integer. `files` stays `uint32` — a declared scope holding more than four billion FILES is not a case this wire owes representation for, and the pair's asymmetry is deliberate. Shared as a vocabulary because the input manifest and both artifact forms carry the SAME record (JTD has no cross-file refs, G9).

The domain-separated algorithm name — `sha256:vibe-input-manifest-v1` for a declared-input manifest, `sha256:file-v1` for a regular file, `sha256:tree-v1` for a directory. The name is part of the witness: two digests of the same bytes under different framings are not comparable.
`sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex characters — the digest the named algorithm produced over its declared scope.
How many regular files entered the manifest. Present for the manifest form, absent for the artifact forms that count nothing.

How many content bytes entered the manifest — a CANONICAL unsigned decimal string (nonempty ASCII digits, no leading zero unless the whole value is `0`). A string because JTD has no `uint64` and a declared input set may exceed 4 GiB; no reader on either side narrows it. Present exactly where `files` is: a count pair is one claim about scope, not two independent numbers.

The run one verification claim was observed under — the identity half PROP-054 `##VERIFY-EVIDENCE-IDENTITY` names first. It is the same run header `.vibe/lifecycle.toml` records, restated on the evidence wire so a reader joins a claim to an invocation without opening machine state. A private supporting fragment: nothing outside `verification_evidence` pulls it, and it exists because JTD cannot express a nested definition shared by two roots.
The durable run identity — exactly 32 lowercase hex characters, the same id the lifecycle state and the compile trace hold themselves to.

The selected workspace node the run was authored by: `.` for the root, or a forward-slashed workspace-relative member path. Part of the identity: the same execution under a different selected node measured a different tree.
The phase the user asked for. It is one of `chain` — a request outside its own chain would name a run that never ran.
The requested full phase chain, in order. Explicit even when it holds one phase; a run with no chain is not a run.
When the run began, in the state file's own spelling — carried verbatim rather than reparsed, so the evidence header and `.vibe/lifecycle.toml` cannot disagree about one run's start.

One declared-input comparison row: the execution whose declared inputs were measured, the declaration it was measured against, and what the measured and the currently observed manifests say. The identity members (`execution`, `phase`, `declaration_fingerprint`, `patterns`) are the claim's scope — PROP-054 `##EVIDENCE-SCOPE-IS-DECLARED`: a tree witness certifies the byte set those patterns select, never the machine. `measured` comes from durable execution state, `observed` is recomputed at verify; which of them is present is what the row's `status` means, and the `comparison-shape` law spells the matrix. This is deliberately NOT the durable state record: `.vibe/lifecycle.toml` stores a measurement (identity plus ONE witness), this stores a comparison, and the two shapes are pinned against each other by a wire test rather than fused into a member nobody could read honestly.
The provider-qualified execution reference (`org.group/pkg#id`) whose declared inputs this row is about.
The lifecycle phase that execution ran in — `build`, `test`, `create`, `verify` or any other phase spelling the chain carries.

`sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex over the execution's declaration. Its sibling, not its alias, is the input manifest digest: the declaration fingerprint answers «is this the same declared work?», the manifest answers «are these the same declared bytes?» (PROP-054 §1.2 of the R7.5 architecture).

The project-relative glob patterns the execution declared, verbatim and in declaration order. EXPLICIT even when empty: an authored empty list is a complete empty declared scope, and it must stay distinguishable from an ABSENT declaration, which is `unavailable` and never a digest of the empty set.
This row's comparison outcome. The root's own status is the worst of every row's, never an independent claim.

The run that produced `measured` — 32 lowercase hex. Present EXACTLY when `measured` is: the id and the witness are one fact, so a row carries both or neither. Absent only where there is no measurement to attribute at all (a legacy state file, or an execution that declared no inputs), which `comparison-shape` grants to `unavailable` alone.
The manifest witness durable state recorded when the execution ran. Absent exactly when the measurement itself is what is unavailable.
The manifest witness recomputed under the current selected world at verify. Absent when the declared scope could not be observed at all — a missing path, or a source that moved while it was read.

A bounded, nonblank machine reason for a non-`matched` row. Required for `missing`, `unavailable` and `unstable` — a status without a reason is a refusal that says nothing — forbidden for `matched`, and optional (but never blank) for `stale`, whose reason is the digests themselves.

One artifact comparison row: the declared artifact's identity (`id`, `kind`, `path`), the witness state recorded when it was produced or fresh-probed, and the witness recomputed at verify. PROP-054 `##EVIDENCE-ARTIFACT-WITNESS`: existence alone never proves freshness, so a row with no `observed` witness is `missing` or `unstable`, never `matched`; and an artifact that was never witnessed (legacy output) is `unavailable` with a reason, not a silent pass. The same `comparison-shape` matrix rules this row and the input row — one law, two carriers, because JTD cannot say «these two records share their comparison half».
The artifact id the producing execution declared.

The artifact kind as the producing contribution spelled it (`file`, `directory`, and whatever else a provider declares) — carried verbatim, never narrowed: the witness algorithm is what says how it was hashed.

The artifact's canonical PROJECT-RELATIVE forward-slashed path under `run.selected` (PROP-054 `##EVIDENCE-ARTIFACT-WITNESS`). Durable lifecycle state keeps the absolute machine path it needs to reopen the file; this external row carries the portable half, because the selected node together with the relative path is the exact identity and an absolute path would leak the operator's home into a published document. The claim is about THIS path's content; a witness recomputed at another path is another claim.
This row's comparison outcome, under the same closed vocabulary and the same matrix as an input row.

The run that produced `measured` — 32 lowercase hex. Present EXACTLY when `measured` is, under the same one-fact rule the input row carries: absent only for the unwitnessed legacy artifact, which is `unavailable`.
The content witness durable state recorded when the artifact was produced or fresh-probed.
The content witness recomputed at verify. Absent when the path is gone, is not a regular file or directory any more, is physically aliased, escapes the project, or moved while it was read.
A bounded, nonblank machine reason for a non-`matched` row, under the same presence rules the input row carries.

The ONE generated verification-evidence member (PROP-054 §14.7, `##EVIDENCE-WIRE-AND-SURFACES`): the lifecycle library produces it, the existing generated `LifecycleReport` carries it, and `vibe verify --json` and MCP `lifecycle_run({phase:"verify"})` return that same value — terminal text is a projection, never a second assembly. `observed_at` is EXCLUDED from `evidence_id`; the id is a domain-separated digest over every other canonical identity and comparison member, so re-reading the same claim at another wall-clock second does not mint a new identity. The relational laws JTD cannot express are named in `x-relational-laws` and enforced by the hand-written validator in `vibe-wire/src/behaviour/verification_evidence/`; the two label sets are pinned equal by a wire test, so an undocumented law and an unimplemented label are both red — the seam the compile-trace member already carries.
x-relational-laws: evidence-identity: `evidence` is exactly 1 (the epoch this member speaks), and `evidence_id` is `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex characters. The writer's digest recipe lands with the writer; the SHAPE of an identity is this wire's own law, because a reader joins claims by that string

run-identity: `run.run_id` is exactly 32 lowercase hex — the same law the lifecycle state and the trace index hold the id to; `run.selected` is `.` or a safe forward-slashed workspace-relative path (nonblank, no backslash, no control byte, no leading `/`, no drive letter, no `.`, `..` or empty segment); `run.requested` and `run.started` are nonblank, bounded and control-free; `run.chain` is nonempty and EVERY phase in it is nonblank, bounded and control-free; `run.requested` is one of `run.chain`

measurement-identity: `measured_run_id` is present EXACTLY when `measured` is — on an input row and an artifact row alike, and whatever the row's status — and when present it is exactly 32 lowercase hex. Neither half stands alone: a `measured` witness with no id is a measurement nobody can be held to, and an id with no witness attributes a measurement the row itself says does not exist, which a reader joining evidence by run id would follow to a claim that was never made. WHICH statuses may take the absent branch is `comparison-shape`'s, and it grants that to `unavailable` alone. Every input row's `declaration_fingerprint` is `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex: a claim measured against an unnameable declaration is not evidence either

witness-shape: every present witness names a nonblank `algorithm` and a `digest` of `sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex, and its `bytes`, when present, is a CANONICAL unsigned decimal string (nonempty ASCII digits, no leading zero unless the value is `0`) — never narrowed through a machine integer. `files` and `bytes` are one pair: within a single witness both are present or both are absent. Which way that goes is decided by the ROW, not by the writer: an input row's witnesses are manifests and MUST carry the pair, an artifact row's witnesses are file/tree digests and MUST NOT, so `matched` can never compare a counted manifest against an uncounted one

comparison-shape: the per-row status matrix. `matched` carries both witnesses, equal in algorithm, digest and both counts, and NO reason code. `stale` carries both witnesses whose compared values differ, and any reason it carries is nonblank. `missing` carries `measured`, carries no `observed`, and carries a nonblank reason. `unavailable` carries NO `measured` — the measurement is what is unavailable — and carries a nonblank reason; it is the ONLY status that may have no measurement. `unstable` carries `measured` (something WAS measured; the re-observation is what was refused), carries no `observed`, and carries a nonblank reason

overall-status: with no rows at all the root status is `unavailable` — an empty evidence set is visible, never a silent pass. Otherwise the root status EQUALS the worst row under the precedence `unstable` > `missing` > `stale` > `unavailable` > `matched`, so `matched` at the root requires a nonempty set every row of which is `matched`

row-identity: input rows are keyed by `execution` and artifact rows by `id`; each key is nonblank and appears at most once. Two rows for one identity would leave a reader with two answers to the same question and no rule for choosing

pattern-safety: every declared pattern is a nonblank project-relative glob spelling — no backslash, no control byte, no leading `/`, no drive letter, and no `.`, `..` or EMPTY segment. A pattern that escapes the project, or that spells one scope two ways, is a scope this wire may not certify

path-safety: every artifact `path` is a safe project-relative forward-slashed path under `run.selected`, by the same grammar the patterns answer to — absolute paths, drive prefixes, backslashes, control bytes and `.`/`..`/empty segments are all refused. Durable state keeps the absolute machine path; the published row carries the portable one, and P2 performs the one normalisation between them

bounded-identity: every identity and diagnostic scalar (`evidence_id`, the run header, `execution`, `phase`, `declaration_fingerprint`, `id`, `kind`, `path`, `algorithm`, `digest`, `reason_code`) is at most the shared diagnostic cap (`x-diagnostic-cap-bytes`) and carries no CR, LF or NUL, and every IDENTITY scalar among them is also nonblank — an unnamed phase or an unnamed artifact kind is an unjoinable claim. A report is a file on disk, so every scalar in it is untrusted text

metadata.description: The evidence wire epoch — 1 today. A reader that does not know the number stops rather than guessing at the members.

`sha256:` followed by 64 lowercase hex over every canonical identity and comparison member EXCEPT `observed_at`. Two reads of the same claim carry the same id; a claim about another tuple carries another one.
The overall comparison outcome — the worst row, never an independent verdict, and never the command's own `ok` (a verify handler may fail while the identity matched).
When the comparison was performed. Excluded from `evidence_id` on purpose: the clock is an input, not part of what was measured.
The run this comparison was observed under.
The declared-input comparison rows, in canonical row order. Explicit even when empty — an empty evidence set is the `unavailable` root, said out loud.
The artifact comparison rows, in canonical row order. Explicit even when empty, for the same reason `inputs` is.
`[boot_snippet]` projection (PROP-005 §2.6): a boot file identified by its `source` path plus an ordering `category`.
Ordering band for the computed boot sequence — `foundation` / `flow` / `stack` / `user-override`.
Compatibility projection: the reader floor and the kinds this record requires.
Reader floor; an absent key declares no floor.
Conflicts projection: packages this version cannot coexist with.
Feature table: feature names map to activation lists; `exclusive` is the at-most-one-of named-group table.
I18n availability: the locales a package carries and its default one.
Default locale; absent when the package declares none.
Obsoletes projection: packages this version replaces.
Provides projection: the capabilities this version exposes.
One any-of requirement: the list IS the entry, so an empty list is emitted, never omitted.
Requires projection: the packages and capabilities this version needs, all of them.
Subskill delivery projection (PROP-005 §2.6).
The package this subskill describes; absent when it is not bound to one.
Human-readable summary; absent when the subskill carries none.
`[origin]` projection (PROP-007 §2.8): provenance of a copy published from a workspace member. `generated_at` is a plain ISO-8601 string in code, not a domain timestamp.
Workspace HEAD the copy was generated from; absent for an uncommitted tree.

Per-version catalog record (PROP-005 §2.6) — one line of `primary.jsonl`, one element of a `by-name` candidate's `versions[]`, one `POST /v1/packages` body. Shared as a vocabulary because `by_name` and `journal` carry it transitively and JTD has no cross-file refs (G9).
Commit the ref resolved to at publish time; absent for non-git sources.
SPDX expression; absent when the package declares none.
Human-readable summary; absent when the package declares none.
Project URL; absent when the package declares none.
PURL of the package this record describes; absent when unbound.

Epoch-1 compiler IR wire: the six manager carriers of PROP-054 §7.4/§14.6, frozen from the landed R3 domain types. One whole value of the level being passed crosses per invocation (`##WHOLE-IR-WIRE`); source/document are one addressed document, documents is the explicit document batch, closure/lane/emitted are one complete final artifact (`##IR-LEVELS`, SPEC-DEBT §8.8). The same document is the R3.4 trace snapshot — no second trace-only IR shape exists. TWO metadata sets sit below and must not be confused: `x-conversion-gates` is what the strict domain decoder OWES on every carrier it is handed, including one a plugin transformed and returned; `x-corpus-producer-oracles` is characterization of what THIS corpus's builtin passes emitted. A plugin may legally return a verifier-valid closure whose anchors the builtin `qualify` would have spelled differently or whose order the builtin `close` would not have chosen — the decoder must accept it, and only the corpus tests hold it to the builtin spelling.
x-conversion-gates: ir_schema == 1 at the manager gate before any invoke, and level/cardinality equal the variant they ride (belt: each is a single-value enum, so a mismatch is already reader-red)

every id is non-blank and free of newline/NUL (`ArtifactId`, `ContributionMeta`, `SourceFormatId`, origins, paths, and a `document_subject`'s `declared_path` plus every `document_provider` coordinate component); a `declared_path` is additionally forward-slashed, since `\` is not a separator to a `paths` selector glob; `BackendId` also matches the id charset
the artifact id/target/frame/mode tuple is one `ArtifactContext::new` row, and a `static-lane` generated_path carries the target's extension
a normal/hoisted contribution's origin coordinate equals its target package coordinate; a hoisted target is an unversioned whole document (no version, no anchor, no pin)
every digest is 64 lowercase hex characters; emitted bytes are canonical padded standard base64 — both validated BEFORE any allocation from them
`raw` re-parses to the authority/doc_path/anchor/pinned_r carried beside it, and a fence delimiter is exactly one character

ARENA BOUNDS, checked before indexing: every `doc_node.parent`, `doc_node.children[]` and `doc_tree.anchors` value is < `doc_tree.nodes.len()`; every closure `seed`, `edge.from`/`edge.to`, occurrence `node` and lane `node` is < the node arena length (`lane.source_node_count` for a lane)

FOREST, checked iteratively and before any descent — total, so no input reaches an index: (a) `doc_tree.nodes` is NON-EMPTY, a typed violation rather than the panic `DocTree::root()` would take, since `DocTree::parse` always mints the synthetic root; (b) node 0 IS that root — level 0, kind `heading`, no `parent` member, no incoming child edge; (c) every non-root node has exactly ONE incoming child edge, claims that parent back (`nodes[c].parent == p` for every `c` in `nodes[p].children`), and is reachable from the root; (d) the walk carries a step bound of `nodes.len() + 1` so a `children` cycle is reported, never followed. Bounds alone are not enough — `DocTree::facts_under` pops a `children` stack and a cycle makes it LOOP FOREVER rather than panic, and a detached ring passes every count while no walk can reach it

SPAN BOUNDS, checked before slicing: `span.start <= span.end <= doc_tree.lines.len()` for every node, and `heading_line < lines.len()` for every non-root node of a non-empty document — `DocTree::text` slices `lines[span]` and panics rather than erroring on an out-of-range value
`doc_tree.anchors[a]` names a node whose `id` is `a`, and each `duplicate_anchors` entry is an anchor that repeats

SET PROJECTION: a member projecting a domain `BTreeSet<String>` (`source_resolution_snapshot.explicit_use_keys`, `embed_resolution_snapshot.explicit_use_keys`) carries its canonical sorted, duplicate-free spelling — otherwise wire→domain→wire silently renormalises and the round-trip is lossy

qualification and absorption typestate align; any planned/applied absorption carries no pending source/embed snapshot, one exact identity-bound plan witness per contribution in order, and each applied normal emission order is exactly the non-absorbed occurrence projection
a link result carries one witness per contribution in order, and a lane brackets each normal occurrence as open/node/[forced-newline]/close with one continuous fence history per contribution

PASS/SNAPSHOT: an `embed` edge exists only once `pending_embeds` is consumed and a `source` edge only once `pending_sources` is — each pass mints its edge kind and clears its own snapshot in one run, so the two can never coexist in any carrier a decoder is handed

EMIT IDENTITY: `target` and `backend` are one id and `producer` is `emit:<backend>`; the artifact id is the one this context ROW rides — equal to the backend id for a builtin static lane and for the custom compatibility row, and the reserved `static-fragment` for the BUILTIN compatibility fragment the `static-md` backend renders. A builtin tape is valid UTF-8 in the framing its OWN emitter writes: a static lane carries the context-owned header/preamble prologue and the ordered contribution markers its emission witnesses declare, while a compatibility fragment carries flattened reversible Markdown with neither of those. Opaque bytes ride a custom target under the compatibility frame. Finally, `bytes_digest` is `independent_bytes_digest(bytes)` = SHA-256 of `le64(26) ‖ "vibe-spec/emitted-bytes/v1" ‖ le64(len) ‖ bytes` — the one digest computable from the wire document alone, so a decoder recomputes it rather than trusting it
x-corpus-producer-oracles: CLOSE ORDER: for a value the BUILTIN `close` produced, TWO witnesses, in this order. (1) EDGE — the `kind == use` edge vector is RECONSTRUCTED from the carried directives, not trusted: per normal contribution in contribution order, walk the reached nodes in traversal order, take each node's OWN `tree.directives.directives`, keep `kind == use`, sort by `line` stably as `use_graph::use_addresses` does, resolve each target by PINLESS address identity to the one carried spec node (missing or ambiguous is a fault, never an index), and append `(from, to, requested_target)` unless that exact tuple is already present — `close.rs:146-197`, where a byte-identical repeat is suppressed while a request differing in pin or raw stays its own edge. Compare to the carrier's vector in exact order and exact requested-target fields; `source`/`embed` edges from later passes are outside this comparison. (2) ORDER — replay `topology::order_by` on the adjacency DERIVED in (1), never on the carrier's edges, and compare node-for-node with the pre-absorb order (the applied plan's occurrences, else the live `emission_order`): declaration-order DFS, Gray/Black colouring, postorder, a Gray target admitted only when it and every node on the current loop suffix is a `contract/…` document (`topology.rs:41-49`). Exact, not merely valid — a legal topological permutation the builtin would not have chosen is still a corpus regression, and deriving the adjacency is what stops (2) from proving only that the order agrees with whatever edges the carrier claims. Two consequences no index comparison could express: the admitted A↔B contract cycle orders `[b, a]` while carrying the edge `0 -> 1`, and two roots sharing nodes yield `[0,1,2]` and `[1,0,3]` from their own declaration orders

Nothing is claimed about a node qualify SKIPPED: an absorbed or already-seen occurrence keeps whatever its author wrote, which may itself look like a slug

OPAQUE TAPE: the emitted golden's `bytes_b64` decodes to `00 ff 0a` — the exact three bytes `OpaqueTestBackend::new` returns (`emit/opaque_test_vehicle.rs`) — under backend `opaque-test`. Characterization of THIS corpus, never a decode rule: any tape whose EMIT IDENTITY coherence holds is a valid carrier

The typed provider identity a document subject carries (`DocumentProvider`, PROP-054 `##CONTRIB-SELECTOR`): the value a source/document selector's `packages` dimension is matched against, spelled as typed coordinate components rather than a rendered display string. The carrier is TOTAL — every document names one arm, and there is no missing-key spelling of absence. The four coordinate arms mirror the kernel's dependency-coordinate and host shapes exactly (`DependencyProviderId`; `HostIdentity`'s ungrouped / coordinate / virtual-workspace spellings), so a match-time adapter reconstructs the typed identity without parsing anything. The two remaining arms are the two DIFFERENT absences, and a full-IR plugin must be able to tell them apart: `unclaimed` says no owner exists to name, `undetermined` says an owner exists and was not resolved. Collapsing them would hand a selector adapter one input for two verdicts.

No contribution row declared this document into this artifact, so no provider is claimed. A PERMANENT and correct answer: the address' authority names the package that owns the document, which is not the question a `packages` dimension asks. An authored `packages` dimension matching nothing is the final verdict here, not a placeholder. Every document the compiler REACHED through `#use`, `#source` or `#embed` carries this arm.

A contribution row DID declare this document, and the producer could not determine which typed provider that row names. A TEMPORARY answer, and the one every document written by today's producers carries: they receive the declaring owner as a display string, and the typed identity reaches the subject only through the owner-view adapter. A selector adapter may not read it as `unclaimed`'s matches-nothing — the honest reading is that the answer is not yet known.
An installed dependency provider's versionless coordinate.
A host project with no group, named exactly as authored.
A grouped project or package-role host, carrying the same validated coordinate a dependency does.
A coordinator that may control dependencies but declares none; it has no coordinate components.

The immutable selector subject of ONE addressed document (`DocumentSubject`): the provider a source/document selector's `packages` dimension matches and the path its `paths` dimension matches. Per addressed document, never per artifact. It is CARRIED, not re-derived — a contribution's `declared_path` is the path the contributing row declared and may legitimately differ from its address' `doc_path` — and the inter-pass verifier refuses a source/document transform that rewrites either member. Required: a decoder refuses a carrier that omits it rather than inventing one, because an invented subject would silently change which transforms a document is in scope for.

The document's declared path, forward-slashed and case-sensitive (the selector adapter contract). Conversion rejects a blank or newline-bearing value, and also a backslashed one: the kernel compiles a `paths` glob with a literal separator, so `\` is not a separator to any pattern and a backslashed path silently matches nothing. The refusal is a refusal, never a normalisation — rewriting the separator would invent an identity the producer did not state.
